label: early input-phase w/d/c/0/e/b/u/a after a sequence starting with r/p/l/y/1/2/g/k
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase (99% of mass), mostly at positions 2-5 (peak at t=3), and almost never at t=0/1, the delimiter, or the copy phase. It acts like a sum of graded factors, not a sharp rule. (1) The current input token: w is by far the strongest (10x lift, 38% of mass), then d, c, 0, e, and more weakly b, u, a. It is mostly the first occurrence of that token (in_first, 95% of mass). (2) Earlier context: activation is boosted when the first token (or earlier tokens such as prev2) is r (strongest, 6x), p, l, y, 1, 2, g or k. The top examples all start with r and have w at t=3. (3) Position: early positions are favoured. No single conjunction captures it. The current token alone gives about 0.79 mass recall at about 0.16 precision; adding the first-token context raises precision to about 0.31-0.43 but loses recall. The neuron does not fire on copy-phase outputs or on letters like f/q/o/v, and it rarely fires on repeated tokens.
